content.text:
I've submitted index 11 (Bi 0.26, Cu 0.24, V 0.49) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I could measure, 1.98e-5 A. Three samples is a very small share of the 117-composition library, so this is the best of what I measured, not necessarily the best in the library.

With so few measurements I spread them across three different regions of the library:

| Index | Composition (Bi/Cu/V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | 0.26 / 0.24 / 0.49 (V-rich, close to BiVO4 with some Cu) | **1.98e-5 A** |
| 0 | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 (equal Bi and V, least Cu) | 1.00e-5 A |
| 64 | 0.05 / 0.57 / 0.38 (mostly copper vanadate, little Bi) | 0 A |

The results suggest the V-rich, BiVO4-like region is the most active and the copper-rich region is inactive. With no measurements left, that trend is untested near index 11.

- **XRD not used:** I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I didn't check which crystal phases are present.
- **Phase list not read:** the known-phases list was too large to return, and I didn't read the file it was saved to.
- **Composition choice:** I picked the compositions to measure from general knowledge of this oxide family, not from structural data.
